publications.title: Integration of counter shaft shedding mechanism into indigenous two-heddle loom: A novel approach
publications.abstract: The study integrates a countershaft shedding mechanism into an indigenous two-heddle loom. It uses observation, interviews and studio experiments to compare conceptual designs. The paper reports use of WeavePoint 7.2 to prepare the weave, draft, lifting/stepping order and tie-up, followed by test weaving.
publications.datasetOrArtifact: WeavePoint 7.2 drafts and physical test-weave samples
publications.verificationNotes: Official journal article page and accessible article content checked. The issue is Vol. 5 No. 1 (2024); some index pages report differing online publication dates. DOI, journal, volume and pages verified. The article concerns a modified indigenous two-heddle loom, not a direct specification of the Bonwire narrow-strip loom.
publications.relevanceNote: Direct Ghanaian precedent for digital weave planning linked to loom operations and physical test weaving. It rules out claiming novelty merely for image-to-draft translation; it does not establish a Kente-specific computational grammar.
publications.researchMethod: Mixed methods: observation of weaving practice, interviews with local weavers and textile experts, studio design experiments, and test weaving.
publications.keyFindings: WeavePoint 7.2 used for weave, draft, lifting/stepping order and tie-up; a modified indigenous two-heddle loom with countershaft shedding was physically tested.
publications.limitations: The work is about loom modification and weaving efficiency, not a formal computational representation of Asante Kente motifs or traditional narrow-strip operation.

publications.title: Analysis of Woven Fabric Structure from Integrated Countershaft Shedding Mechanism on an Indigenous Handloom
publications.abstract: The study evaluates a countershaft shedding mechanism integrated into an indigenous Ghanaian handloom. A modified indigenous four-post handloom was used to produce fabrics across four-to-six shaft configurations, including plain derivatives, twills, diamonds and satin structures. Mechanical fabric testing and qualitative artisan evaluation involved master weavers from Bonwire and Agortime-Kpetoe.
publications.datasetOrArtifact: Physical woven fabric samples and artisan evaluation
publications.verificationNotes: Official Fashion and Textiles Review article page and abstract checked; published 14 April 2026, Volume 7, pages 67–83. DOI verified. Data sharing is stated to be available upon reasonable request. The modified four-to-six-shaft countershaft setup must not be equated with the traditional Bonwire narrow-strip loom.
publications.relevanceNote: Provides a recent Ghanaian precedent for physical fabric production, structural/mechanical testing and artisan evaluation involving Bonwire weavers. It helps ground validation feasibility but does not itself provide a Kente-specific computational grammar or narrow-strip loom operation specification.
publications.researchMethod: Mixed methods: experimental fabric production, tensile testing, drape/structural assessment and qualitative surveys/expert evaluation with master weavers.
publications.keyFindings: Multi-shaft weave structures include plain derivatives, twills, diamonds and satin; the paper reports changes in fabric properties, pattern precision and weaver experience.
publications.limitations: The setup is a modified four-post countershaft handloom with four-to-six shafts. Its operations and findings cannot be transferred automatically to a traditional narrow-strip loom or assumed to represent all Asante Kente structures.
